articles.summary: Red Bull's Max Verstappen wins an extraordinary Las Vegas Grand Prix that featured 34 lead changes and another collision between the Ferraris.
articles.body:
Red Bull's Max Verstappen won an extraordinary Las Vegas Grand Prix that featured 34 lead changes in a non-stop battle at the front.

The leading group of 10 cars were tied together for the vast majority of the race as the lead constantly changed hands between Verstappen and the Mercedes drivers George Russell and Kimi Antonelli.

But Verstappen was the one constant, always seeming a step ahead of his rivals as he debated electrical energy deployment strategy with his team.

And in the final laps Mercedes' challenge unravelled as first Russell made a mistake and crashed trying to pass Antonelli, and the Italian lost out to the two McLarens of Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri going into the final lap.

The world champion dropped to fifth going on to the Strip on the last lap but was able to reclaim the place from Alpine's Pierre Gasly at the end of the long straight.

And there was more drama at Ferrari as Charles Leclerc earned a 10-second penalty for tipping Lewis Hamilton into a spin.

Earlier, Hamilton had been given a 10-second penalty of his own for passing Norris off the track in a fight for position that also involved Leclerc.

It was a grand prix more reminiscent of American oval racing than Formula 1, and it depended on unique circumstances revolving around the Las Vegas circuit and energy-starved hybrid engines this year.

But there was no questioning the showbiz value in the city that prides itself as the entertainment capital of the world.

The key stories of an engrossing race were:

Verstappen's remarkable intelligence and control in the lead in the most demanding of circumstances

Another dip in a dreadful season for Russell

More controversy at Ferrari, as both drivers earned 10-second penalties for driving infringements in battles involving the other

Verstappen a constant amid chaos as he says Russell is 'so far below my level'

Hamilton-Leclerc collision 'completely unacceptable'

Verstappen's superb racecraft & Russell's costly mistake - driver ratings

"How many overtakes did I do?" Verstappen asked his engineer on the slowing down lap, as he reflected on a race the like of which F1 has not seen since the famous Monza slipstreaming battles of the 1960s and early 1970s.

"Yeah, and not many of them on the straight," his new engineer Tom Hart said, summing up how Verstappen had secured the win against the Mercedes challenge.

Lap after lap after lap, Verstappen, who started from pole, would lose the lead to Russell on the Strip only to reclaim it at the last corner, usually going around the outside.

If that did not work, and Russell passed later in the lap, or led across the line, Verstappen developed a trademark move around the outside of Turn Three to get back in front.

The race went on and on like that, punctuated by a mid-grand prix safety car, but through it all Verstappen always seemed in control.

As the race wore on, Antonelli came into the picture after starting sixth, and passed Russell with 12 laps to go to become Verstappen's main challenger.

Now it was the Italian's turn to swap places with Verstappen, but again the Dutchman had the measure of Mercedes.

At one point, Verstappen asked his team to come up with a better deployment strategy for the final lap because he thought Mercedes had "figured it out".

They came back to him to say that he had already come up with the best approach.

In the end, though, he need not have worried, as his rivals behind him gave him enough of a gap at the start of the final lap to not have to worry too much about defending his lead.

That critical final phase started with Russell deciding to make a move to become Verstappen's challenger again.

Russell went for a move into Turn Five with two laps to go but he locked up his brakes over the bumps heading into the corner - bumps that had earlier taken Red Bull's Isack Hadjar out of the lead battle when his front wing broke over them - and went straight on into the barrier.

Russell managed to reverse out of the barrier, but a ninth-place finish was not what he was expecting.

The incident was also unfortunate for him in the context of his calling out Verstappen's driving after qualifying, when he said "somebody has got to stand up to that guy".

Verstappen had the last word, both on track and literally. After seeing Russell's embarrassing mistake, Verstappen came on the radio to say: "Hah, hah. Well done. My God."

Now Antonelli looked to be the man who would challenge Verstappen for the win.

But that was counting without the McLarens. Piastri had already driven an outstanding race to recover from starting 17th because of an engine penalty and Norris had at one point dropped out of the top 10 in the chaotic lead battle in the first part of the grand prix.

But they were third and fourth around the penultimate lap and both swept around Antonelli around the outside of the fast final corner heading into the last lap.

Antonelli had lifted off the throttle because he wanted to stay behind Verstappen and attack him later, but in so doing had triggered a setting in the engine defined by the rules that left him without battery power.

It deprived him of the chance to deploy what Mercedes team boss Toto Wolff said was a "secret" deployment strategy on the final lap that he felt would have kept Antonelli ahead through the final corners after passing Verstappen down the Strip.

Instead, it gave Verstappen breathing space, and Antonelli was delayed sufficiently that he could not recover to challenge them.

Second-placed Norris summed it up, saying: "I think that must have been the most chaotic race ever in the history of Formula 1. I didn't know what was happening half the time."

A hectic end to the season means Formula 1 moves from Las Vegas to the Middle East next weekend, for the Qatar Grand Prix at the Lusail International Circuit from 27-29 November.

articles.title: Alonso ni cruza meta: "En las curvas íbamos mejor que los rivales, pero en la recta fue lo peor del año"
articles.standfirst: El asturiano no pudo finalizar la carrera y tuvo que aparcar su Aston Martin en la entrada del pit-lane del Gran Premio de Las Vegas
articles.summary: El asturiano no pudo finalizar la carrera y tuvo que aparcar su Aston Martin en la entrada del pit-lane del Gran Premio de Las Vegas
articles.body: Fernando Alonso no pudo evitar mostrar su enfado al terminar su participación en el Gran Premio de Las Vegas. "El motor se ha roto", repetía por su radio durante la última vuelta de carrera después sufrir una extraña salida en una de las curvas y perder el poco rendimiento que tenía. No terminó una carrera en la que rozó el puesto 16º como tope y en el que se vio resignado a no tener herramientas para pelear. Con un motivo que no se podía ocultar: el motor Honda. Se señalaba que en Las Vegas sufriría más que en todos los demás con permiso de Monza y Bakú, y el caos fue total en un coche que no se comportaba mal en las pocas curvas del Strip. "Íbamos mejor que el resto en curva, el coche se comportaba muy bien. Pero en las rectas ha sido la peor carrera del año", explica el asturiano a la prensa internacional. Y en Las Vegas todo son rectas. Ni ayudó una buena salida, en la que se tiró a un Piastri que terminó subiendo al podio en remontada. Y tampoco pelear ante los Haas, Cadillac y su compañero Stroll mientras por delante se sucedían los líos. "No luchaba, perdía dos o tres segundos en las rectas. Lograba ganar tiempo en curvas e intentaba seguir al pelotón", aclara Alonso. Que buscaba pelear en el frío y la baja temperatura de neumáticos. "Estuvo bien para nosotros. Obviamente, la primera vuelta fue complicada, al igual que la primera vuelta tras la salida del coche de seguridad, pero una vez que los neumáticos alcanzaron la temperatura adecuada, fue bastante bien", añade. Que también reconoce que la unidad de potencia no estaba bien: "Fallaba desde el inicio de carrera. Ya en la clasificación vimos que fallaba y ha estado así toda la carrera. Perdía mucho tiempo. No sólo con el resto, también con Lance [Stroll]". Hasta el desenlace en el que su frustración apareció con un brutal bloqueo en la entrada a boxes. "El motor se rindió por completo", sentencia. Dejándole otra carrera de infortunio y mal rendimiento que ni la lucha del piloto pudo cambiar. Su octavo abandono de la temporada, aunque la estadística le dejará en el puesto 19 al haber cruzado la meta en todas las vueltas anteriores. Una carrera menos para el 2027.

articles.title: Ferrari estalla tras el toque de Leclerc a Hamilton y estudia tomar medidas disciplinarias
articles.standfirst: El monegasco pasó la línea roja al tocar al británico y la catarata de reacciones es total
articles.summary: El monegasco pasó la línea roja al tocar al británico y la catarata de reacciones es total
articles.body: YFerrari... terminó de estallar. Tal y como se veía venir, sin importar aquella paz que no era más que algunas palabras vacías que no resuelven nada. Probablemente, tampoco lo haga la pista en una cuestión de estado en la Scuderia con importancia en los despachos de la Gestione Sportiva, la fábrica y su gente. Y en Las Vegas, la situación explotó con el toque de Charles Leclerc a Lewis Hamilton que cortó sus opciones hasta un pobre 7º -del 44- y 10º final. No sólo hubo movida en un giro 38 que recordarán durante tiempo. Ya venían de no pasar a la Q3 en la clasificación y durante la carrera empezó la tensión con una sanción a Hamilton por sacar ventaja fuera de límites de pista. Antes, Leclerc no dejó de atacarle y la retahíla de comentarios del británico llegó. Pero todavía habría más. En el tramo final de carrera se encontraban juntos y Ferrari pidió a Leclerc no atacar. Pero el monegasco se tomó la justicia por la mano, lanzó el coche y tocó al británico al no tener espacio. Terminó sancionado y la crisis se desató. "Quiero que vengas a hablar conmigo antes de nada", pedía su jefe, Fred Vasseur. El golpe era total, perdiendo fuelle en el subcampeonato (304 puntos de Verstappen, 267 de Hamilton, 264 de Russell y Norris, y 250 de Leclerc). Porque era una acción reincidente y otro golpe a la confianza de un equipo en guerra. "Vamos a tomar decisiones. También consideramos multar o medidas disciplinarias. Es inaceptable poner este esfuerzo y recursos para que pasen cosas así", explicaba el dirigente francés. Que no se podía explicar la situación entre sus pilotos. "Me tenéis que creer. Es muy difícil de aceptar esto. Todos estamos molestos. Cuando fichamos a Lewis [Hamilton] no pensábamos que pasaría algo así. Tomaremos medidas", añadió. Con el golpe y la desobediencia de Leclerc en el foco. "Le dijimos que no pasase porque se lo devolverían, pero cometió un fallo que ha dañado al equipo y es inaceptable", soltó Vasseur. El monegasco sólo podía dar justificaciones sin importancia. "No es aceptable. No creo que tengamos que discutir algo con Lewis, le diré mi punto de vista pero tengo 10 segundos de sanción. Dentro del coche quizá era demasiado, pero han habido muchas consecuencias", comentó. Por su parte, Hamilton no hurgaba en la herida. Sólo acudía al histórico. "Ferrari tiene que decidir. Yo hice todo lo posible, hablando de todo y más. Es difícil, así que sólo puedo dar todo. Con suerte, quizá se resuelva todo eventualmente", cerró el siete veces campeón.

articles.title: 35 lead changes, 352 overtakes, Max Verstappen's masterclass: Las Vegas GP delivers one of the craziest F1 races of 2026
articles.summary: If Formula One needed a reminder of why it remains one of the most unpredictable forms of motorsport, the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix delivered it in
articles.body: If Formula One needed a reminder of why it remains one of the most unpredictable forms of motorsport, the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix delivered it in spectacular fashion. Under the dazzling lights of the Las Vegas Strip, Max Verstappen emerged victorious from a breathless 50-lap contest that featured 35 lead changes and an astonishing 352 overtakes, making it one of the wildest races of the season.While Verstappen eventually secured the chequered flag, his victory was anything but straightforward. The Red Bull driver had to withstand relentless pressure from Mercedes, survive repeated position exchanges and keep his composure as the race unfolded into a tactical and strategic battle.The four-time world champion crossed the finish line in 1:27:39.624, just 0.639 seconds ahead of McLaren's Lando Norris, while Oscar Piastri completed the podium after producing an impressive recovery drive from 17th on the grid.Slipstreaming turns Las Vegas into an overtaking paradiseThe long straights of the Las Vegas Strip Circuit played a significant role in creating the extraordinary spectacle. The powerful slipstream effect made it difficult for drivers to establish a comfortable lead, allowing rivals to repeatedly close in and attempt overtakes.Verstappen started from pole position and initially maintained control, but George Russell quickly emerged as his biggest challenger. The Mercedes driver repeatedly found opportunities to overtake the Dutchman, only for Verstappen to respond and reclaim the position.The battle between the two became a recurring theme throughout the race, with the lead changing hands multiple times. Kimi Antonelli also entered the fight as Mercedes looked increasingly capable of challenging Red Bull for victory. Even Isack Hadjar briefly found himself in contention before his front wing suffered a failure, forcing him to drop down the order.The result was an extraordinary 35 changes of the lead, while drivers across the field completed 352 overtakes during the 50-lap contest.Safety Car adds another twist as midfield battles intensifyThe drama was not restricted to the leading positions. A collision between Sergio Perez and Rafael Camara brought out the Safety Car during the middle stages of the race, giving teams another opportunity to reassess their strategies.The incident also created opportunities for drivers further down the order to close the gaps. Oscar Piastri, who had started 17th after taking a grid penalty for a new internal combustion engine, began making significant progress through the field. However, McLaren's race was not without complications. Piastri lost valuable track position during the pit-stop sequence and dropped back to 11th before beginning another recovery.The Australian gradually worked his way through the pack, making the most of the battles unfolding ahead of him. His charge eventually brought him into contention for a podium finish. Meanwhile, Hadjar's front-wing failure ended his hopes of challenging the leading drivers, while Arvid Lindblad also suffered a dramatic moment after spinning behind the Safety Car and eventually retiring.Mercedes collapse in dramatic closing laps as Verstappen takes controlThe biggest twist arrived during the closing stages, when Mercedes appeared to have a genuine opportunity to challenge Verstappen for victory. Russell continued to push hard and attempted to overtake his teammate Antonelli with just three laps remaining. However, the British driver locked up, hit the barrier and dropped down the order, eventually finishing ninth.Antonelli also suffered a problem with his energy deployment on the final lap, allowing the McLaren duo to capitalise and move ahead of him.Verstappen, meanwhile, maintained his composure and finally managed to build the advantage he had struggled to establish throughout the race. The Dutchman crossed the finish line to secure his third victory on the streets of Las Vegas, finishing 0.639 seconds ahead of Norris.Ferrari's intra-team collision adds to Las Vegas dramaWhile Red Bull celebrated at the front, Ferrari endured another frustrating evening. Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc were involved in a collision while battling for position with 12 laps remaining. The incident left both drivers facing penalties, with Leclerc receiving a 10-second time penalty for causing the collision.Hamilton had already received a separate 10-second penalty for leaving the track and gaining an advantage during his earlier battle with Norris. Hamilton eventually finished seventh, while Leclerc crossed the line in 10th after his penalty was applied.Carlos Sainz also produced a solid performance for Williams, finishing eighth in his 250th Grand Prix.Despite the late disappointment, Mercedes still had both drivers inside the top 10, with Russell recovering to ninth.Las Vegas Grand Prix 2026: Top 10 race resultsPositionDriverTeamTime / Gap1Max VerstappenRed Bull1:27:39.6242Lando NorrisMcLaren+0.639s3Oscar PiastriMcLaren+1.529s4Kimi AntonelliMercedes+2.574s5Pierre GaslyAlpine+2.927s6Franco ColapintoAlpine+7.955s7Lewis HamiltonFerrari+12.795s8Carlos SainzWilliams+12.938s9George RussellMercedes+13.192s10Charles LeclercFerrari+17.554sGet the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Max Verstappen says George Russell 'so far below his level' after poking fun at rival for major error during Las Vegas GP
articles.summary: Red Bull's Max Verstappen won the Las Vegas Grand Prix and hit out at George Russell after the Mercedes driver said "I'm not going accept somebody to screw me over" after the pair collided in final practice; Russell crashed during Sunday's race and finished down in ninth
articles.body:
Verstappen claimed his fourth win of the season after a stunning defensive drive while Russell crashed in the latter stages and finished ninth, having battled Verstappen for the win earlier.

The pair collided in final practice on Saturday with Verstappen warned for "driving erratically" in the incident but Russell criticised the Red Bull driver.

"There's nothing in the rules to say you cannot overtake someone who is starting a lap but when you do this, you are screwing this person over and he does this week in, week out with many drivers and everybody accepts it," he told Sky Italy .

"I'm not just going to accept somebody to screw me over like this and walk around like they're bigger and better than everyone else. Somebody's got to stand up to that guy."

Verstappen was asked about the comments in the post-race press conference following his third Las Vegas Grand Prix victory and hit back at Russell.

He said: "The thing is, he speaks a lot next to the track. And honestly, for me, it doesn't really bother me because he's so far below my level that it doesn't really make any sense for me anyway to try and challenge that. So, it doesn't bother me.

"And today, karma is a b****. It was honestly fantastic when I looked in my mirror and I saw what was happening [when Russell crashed]. I was like, 'fantastic, my day is only getting better.'

"And of course, when I then crossed the line in first, my day was complete."

Verstappen: Finish would have been tight without Antonelli issue

The battery-sensitive power units and significant slipstream effect created an unusual style of racing, with the field tightly bunched and the leader unable to build a meaningful gap.

Verstappen, however, remained consistently in the top two and revealed that Mercedes pair Russell and Kimi Antonelli had worked out they could pass the Dutchman into Turn 14, potentially setting themselves up to win the race on the final lap.

However, Antonelli dropped from second to fifth on the penultimate lap due to a deployment issue, allowing Verstappen to take a relatively comfortable victory ahead of McLaren duo Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri.

"You put a lot of scenarios in your head and unfortunately with Kimi something went wrong on his side, so we never really got that fight to the line because I'm pretty sure it was going to be a fight to the line," Verstappen told Sky Sports F1 .

"We did well. I wanted to try and stay in the lead instead of dropping back in the pack and making sure we always had the deployment correct to re-overtake when I would be overtake into Turn 14.

"And at the same time, making sure you could be late on the brakes, sending it up the inside or outside, just defending that leading position."

McLaren's double podiums means they have cut their deficit to Red Bull in the battle for third in the Constructors' Championship to 17 points with two rounds remaining in Qatar and Abu Dhabi.

Verstappen said: "We've had a lot of strong races and some races where we have to learn still and do better but that's fine. That's what we are trying to do heading into next year.

"At the same time, there's still a big battle for us for P3 in the Constructors' Championship. In that sense today was not a good day, even with the win, so we have a fight on our hands in the last two rounds."

articles.title: Verstappen y un zasca que retumba: "Russell está tan por debajo de mi nivel..."
articles.standfirst: Le recuerdan las palabras del británico del sábado y contesta que disfrutó el momento en el que se fue contra el muro en carrera
articles.summary: Le recuerdan las palabras del británico del sábado y contesta que disfrutó el momento en el que se fue contra el muro en carrera
articles.body: Parece una situación irreconciliable, que arrancó en Qatar 2024 y sigue coleando hasta este momento. Max Verstappen habló de George Russell en unos términos realmente duros, tras un encontronazo en los libres 3 de Las Vegas y las posteriores palabras de piloto de Mercedes: "Alguien tiene que plantarle cara a este tipo", aseguró en los medios tras un episodio en el que Max le adelantó sin sentido, pero luego estuvo a punto de llevarlo contra el muro sin dejarle espacio. Eso fue el sábado , pero en la rueda de prensa posterior a la carrera a Max le preguntaron por esas afirmaciones de Russell sobre su actitud en la pista, algo que el ganador en Las Vegas aprovechó para hacer sangre y regodearse del error del británico en el tramo final de la carrera. "El caso es que habla mucho fuera de la pista y sinceramente es algo que no me molesta, porque está tan por debajo de mi nivel que ni siquiera intento rebatirle, no es algo que me moleste", comenzaba con un zasca que no se suele ver entre deportistas del más alto nivel. "Y hoy el karma fue muy perro... ha sido fantástico cuando he visto en mi retrovisor lo que le ha pasado, fantástico", señalaba aludiendo a su error en una frenada que le dejó fuera de la pelea por la victoria. Y añadía... "Mi día tan solo estaba mejorando y luego cuando he terminado primero ha sido el colofón", cerraba el holandés sonriendo en todo su discurso. No hay tregua ni va a haberla a corto plazo por lo que parece. Pero es que en la misma carrera, dentro del coche Max dijo por la radio. "¡Ja, ja, bien hecho! Dios mío”, al enterarse del incidente de Russell al frenar por la zona sucia y no poder gestionar la curva.

articles.title: Ferrari boss Frederic Vasseur blames Charles Leclerc for 'unacceptable' collision with Lewis Hamilton in Las Vegas GP
articles.summary: The Ferrari team-mates clashed on track once again, just weeks after their costly collision in Mexico City derailed the team’s race; Charles Leclerc punished by stewards and blamed by team boss Frederic Vasseur after spinning Lewis Hamilton in battle over sixth place
articles.body:
The Ferrari drivers made contact when battling over sixth place with 12 laps remaining in a breathless, frenzied race in which the team were attempting to recover from a poor qualifying when both drivers were knocked out in Q2.

Hamilton was spun around in the Turn Seven-collision, dropping to 10th in the order. Leclerc was found to be at fault by race stewards, who imposed a 10-second penalty on him.

That was applied to Leclerc's final race time and dropped him to 10th place in the final classification, with Hamilton ending up seventh.

Two weeks after speaking to both drivers to remind them of their responsibilities to the team after a squabble on track in Mexico had cost them a likely win, Vasseur was left unimpressed.

"Clearly, it's unacceptable," Vasseur told Sky Italy.

"A little bit the same message as Mexico because you have to think about the team, about the people working in Maranello. About all the stakeholders, the sponsors and so on.

"We told Charles not to overtake, because in a race like this, you have to focus on your own race rather than risk being overtaken by others. Charles clearly made a mistake, and it has cost the team dearly. What happened today [Sunday] is completely unacceptable.

"Honestly, I am more than upset because that message was clear after Mexico.

"We had a chat all together in Brazil. Today we passed the message to think about the team when they were racing together and the outcome is this one. It's mega frustrating for all of us."

'I'm penalised so it has to be my mistake' - Leclerc frustrated but accepts decision

In their report confirming the decision to penalise Leclerc, the stewards said the Monegasque had started his move on Hamilton from "a considerable distance behind" in the sister Ferrari, Hamilton's car, and had "not earned the right to the corner" by the apex.

They therefore found him to be "wholly to blame".

On Leclerc's cool-down lap back to the pits at the end of the race, Vasseur told him on Ferrari team radio: "Charles, I want to see you just after the race, before everything"

While stopping short of any apology in his immediate post-race TV interview, instead saying he was "embarrassed for the team", a visibly-frustrated Leclerc said he accepted the stewards' decision.

"I have been penalised so, as a result, I guess the majority and the stewards thought that it was my mistake. I'll accept that," Leclerc told Sky Sports F1 .

"I'm not going to say much more. At the end of the day, I'm penalised so it has to be my mistake."

Asked if Ferrari now needed to impose stricter rules, Leclerc said: "Well, I just feel quite embarrassed for the team in general. We'll review."

In comments later published in Ferrari's post-race press release, Leclerc added: "The race didn't finish well for us, and my mistake was part of that. I accept the penalty and we will review what I could have done differently so it doesn't happen again. I'm sorry for the team, for everyone in Maranello and for the points we lost today."

'I've done all I can' - will Hamilton's call for change be heeded?

Hamilton had called for rules of engagement between the drivers after an incident between them on the first lap of Ferrari's home race at Monza in September, when he was forced onto the gravel. Leclerc subsequently apologised.

Asked by Sky Sports F1 after Sunday's incident if it was not time for some proper rules, Hamilton shrugged his shoulders and said: "That's for Ferrari to decide, obviously.

"I've done all I can and I've said everything and more.

"It's been difficult. All I can do is just show up and give it everything I can and hopefully in the background they eventually figure it out."

Seemingly fully aware that they risked disadvantaging each other by fighting hard as they both attempted to make their way back up the order from the fringes of the top 10, Hamilton asked the team over the radio "can you tell him to back the f*** off" when they came up to the McLarens.

"I'm not going to get into the scenario of that," he said afterwards. "That's something for you to speak to Ferrari about.

"But we knew that were faced with a massive challenge this weekend. We didn't realise that there'd be such a limitation on these straights.

"Qualifying was obviously difficult but in the race I felt great and I was really progressing well. I really ultimately wanted to try and make sure we finish ahead of the McLarens, because that's who we're really fighting in the constructors'. Then avoiding a collision with one of the McLarens got me a 10-second penalty which was, I think, really harsh and which was frustrating.

"But I just got my head back down and kept chasing and managed to get back in the fight and then again got knocked back again.

"But I never gave up and I was just trying to get the best result. I really think we could have had a podium today with the pace we had."

articles.title: Las Vegas Grand Prix: Ferrari drivers Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc face tense discussion over their ability to race together.
articles.summary: Ferrari drivers Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc face yet another tense discussion over their ability to race together cleanly on track after colliding in Las Vegas.
articles.body:
Ferrari drivers Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc face yet another tense discussion over their ability to race together cleanly on track after colliding in the Las Vegas Grand Prix.

Leclerc tipped Hamilton into a spin with 22 laps to go, costing both points in a race where at one stage they were racing with the McLarens, who finished on the podium.

Leclerc was given a 10-second penalty for the incident, which meant he finished 10th, three places behind Hamilton, in a race won by Red Bull's Max Verstappen.

It was the second race-compromising incident within three grands prix, and it came after the drivers had been brought together to clear the air at the last race in Brazil after their first-lap fighting in Mexico cost them a win.

Hamilton said such an incident "should never happen" but added that: "The question should be for Ferrari now."

Leclerc said: "We just need to fix whatever is not working."

Team principal Frederic Vasseur described the situation as "completely unacceptable".

Verstappen wins extraordinary race as Ferraris collide

Verstappen's superb racecraft & Russell's costly mistake - driver ratings

The Frenchman said: "It's a lack of respect for the team, for the sponsor, the same speech as after Mexico.

"We passed the message to Charles to not overtake because in this kind of race you have to overtake the cars in front of you or you're passed by others. It means you have to do your race and Charles clearly made a mistake.

"It's penalising the team a lot and it's completely unacceptable. Honestly we are more than upset because that message was clear after Mexico, we had a chat together in Brazil, today we passed the message to think about the team when racing together and the outcome is this one."

The battle between the two drivers has been tense all season, and in the second part of the year there have been a series of flashpoints, whether it be on-track racing, disputes about how best to work through strategy, and Hamilton ignoring two separate calls to pit in different races, both of which compromised his result, because he was looking at beating Leclerc.

Hamilton said: "It's not something I want to really get into."

The seven-time champion, who struggled against Leclerc last year but who has been revived in 2026, deflected questions about whether he should be given number-one status.

"I've never asked to be number one," he said. "I genuinely haven't ever asked.

"There was a point in the season where I was 40-odd points ahead, and at that point, the fight was with me and Kimi (Antonelli).

"I was the closest one to him. I was second for a long time in the year.

"At that point, we needed backing to make sure we beat Kimi. There were a few instances in the season where, with the support, I think we could have beaten Kimi.

"But no, that's not what I've asked for. We shouldn't have gotten together. That should just never happen. But I've said everything I can on it, and the question should be for Ferrari now."

Before the incident, the drivers expressed their differing views on team radio, Leclerc expressing his concern for the way Hamilton was defending, Hamilton saying they should be focused on catching the cars in front.

Leclerc said: "He needs to be careful with this squeezing because it's not going to end well."

Hamilton swore as he asked the team to tell Leclerc to "back off", adding: "I'm trying to catch these guys ahead."

This was similar to their different stances in Mexico, when Leclerc was attacking Hamilton on the first lap while the Briton felt they should be working together to defend their one-two positions.

Vasseur said he would talk to the drivers the day after the race, once the immediate heat of the situation had dissipated.

"You can't imagine the frustration for me, but more important for the guys at home," Vasseur said.

"I want to have a discussion tomorrow. Also, Charles to digest the situation. It's not the right place to discuss with them two minutes after the race."

Leclerc said: "I don't think it's going to be intense. None of our discussions were intense, but surely it cannot continue like that.

"I've taken a penalty, so I guess the blame is on me from the stewards and I guess from the majority, so as a result I guess it was deserved."

Analysis: Hamilton v Leclerc becoming unsolvable problem

Hamilton v Leclerc is turning into an unsolvable problem at Ferrari.

For the sake of the team's results, team principal Vasseur needs to find a way to get the two to race together on track in a way that does not constantly undermine the collective result.

McLaren have - mostly - managed it with Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri.

So far, Vasseur has been unable to, or his drivers have not allowed him to. Which explains his response to the latest incident in Las Vegas.

In this case, Vasseur is laying the blame squarely on Leclerc's shoulders. At other times, it has been more nuanced.

Even in Mexico two races ago, that was the case. Hamilton was claiming the moral high ground as the leader - he felt Leclerc should not have attacked him as he did on the opening lap.

But they are allowed to race, and it can also be argued that Hamilton had a share of the blame - had he braked a little earlier, he would have stayed on track, not lost position to Verstappen, and been the beneficiary as Leclerc was forced to hand back the place he had gained by cutting a corner.

Leclerc is in an unfamiliar position - he has always been faster than his team-mates in F1. Now, he finds himself alongside someone matching him.

Hamilton is not - he has had competitive team-mates before, and it has usually not ended well. Ask Fernando Alonso and Nico Rosberg about that.

There were "serious talks" between Hamilton and Leclerc, brokered by Vasseur, earlier this month to solve what Hamilton said were "big problems".

Both drivers said these were now behind them. Clearly they are not. Even when accepting he was at fault, there was a tone to Leclerc's remarks post-Vegas that made it clear he did not believe it was all entirely on him.

They are incredibly evenly matched, and both are determined to be the person who delivers the next title to Ferrari. Fighting like this could well mean neither does, even if the team are ever in a position to win one.

The immovable object meets the irresistible force. What's the solution to that equation?

articles.title: 'So far below my level': Max Verstappen takes brutal swipe at George Russell after Las Vegas GP win

articles.body: Max Verstappen had more than just a race victory to celebrate at the Las Vegas Grand Prix. So it doesn't bother me," Verstappen said.The Dutchman's remarks came after Russell had publicly criticised him following their incident during final practice in Las Vegas. Mercedes teammate Kimi Antonelli also joined the battle, making it a fascinating three-way contest at the front.With just three laps remaining, Russell attempted to overtake Antonelli but locked up under braking and ran into the barriers. Although he managed to recover and rejoin the race, the incident destroyed his chances of fighting for victory, leaving him ninth at the chequered flag.Verstappen, who was watching the drama unfold in his mirrors, admitted that Russell's misfortune made his evening even better."Today, karma is a bitch. It was honestly fantastic when I looked in my mirror and I saw what was happening. So I was like, 'Fantastic! My day is only getting better!'" he said."And of course, when I then crossed the line in first, my day was complete," Verstappen added.Verstappen holds off Mercedes challenge to win Las Vegas GPThe Dutchman had to work hard for his victory despite starting from pole position. Russell repeatedly challenged him for the lead, while Antonelli also managed to move ahead during the 50-lap contest.The race turned into an extraordinary battle, with slipstreaming and repeated overtaking making it difficult for any driver to establish a comfortable advantage.Verstappen eventually crossed the finish line in 1:27:39.624, just 0.639 seconds ahead of McLaren's Lando Norris. articles.title: Las Vegas Grand Prix: Harry Benjamin's driver ratings as Max Verstappen seals victory from pole position
articles.summary: BBC Radio 5 Live F1 commentator Harry Benjamin rates how the drivers performed during the Las Vegas Grand Prix weekend.
articles.body:
Max Verstappen sealed his fourth win of the season with a stunning victory at a chaotic Las Vegas Grand Prix.

The Red Bull driver fought off his rivals for the lead throughout the race and crossed the line ahead of the two McLarens of Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri.

George Russell, who started second, locked up late on attempting a move on Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli and finished ninth, while Charles Leclerc was given a 10-second time penalty for making contact with Ferrari team-mate Lewis Hamilton.

Here are my ratings for how the drivers performed across the whole weekend in Vegas.

A superb display of racecraft. Inherited pole after Kimi Antonelli's grid penalty and spent virtually the entire race being attacked, passed and then finding a way back through, while also working out the optimum energy deployment from inside his Red Bull. One of his finest victories.

A remarkable recovery after dropping as low as 11th in the madness of the opening part of the race. Had genuine pace throughout and fought all the way back to second, finishing less than a second behind Verstappen.

One of the drives of the race. Qualified seventh but started 17th because of his engine penalty and charged all the way through to the podium, gaining 14 places and joining McLaren team-mate Norris in passing Antonelli right at the end.

Fastest of everyone in qualifying and a genuine contender for victory despite starting sixth because of his engine penalty. Battled Verstappen superbly before his Mercedes' energy deployment problem on the final lap cost him two places, although he still recovered fourth from Pierre Gasly before the flag.

An excellent weekend and comfortably Alpine's best result of the season. Reached Q3, stayed with the leading group throughout and was less than three seconds away from victory at the finish.

Another huge result for Alpine. Qualified inside the top 10, stayed out of trouble while plenty around him didn't and converted ninth on the grid into sixth place.

A messy weekend but there was still plenty of fight in the race. Missing Q3 was disappointing and the 10-second time penalty for passing Norris off the circuit was harsh, although being spun by Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc later on was not his fault and he recovered to finish seventh.

A superb recovery from 20th on the grid after his power-unit penalty. Kept himself in contention throughout, made up 12 places and even pinched eighth from Russell at the line to secure Williams' joint-best result of the season.

For 48 laps this was heading towards a very high score. Fastest in both second and final practice, qualified third and spent most of the race going toe-to-toe with Verstappen for the lead. But locking up and putting it into the barrier with two laps remaining was an enormous and costly mistake.

A frustrating weekend from start to finish. Ferrari's qualifying struggles left him 11th and although he recovered well enough to finish sixth on the road, spinning his team-mate Hamilton earned a 10-second time penalty and dropped him to 10th.

Verstappen wins extraordinary race as Ferraris collide

Verstappen a constant amid chaos as he says Russell is 'so far below my level'

Hamilton-Leclerc collision 'completely unacceptable'

A solid weekend without quite finding the points. Led Audi in qualifying and again in the race, eventually finishing 11th after spending much of the evening embroiled in the midfield fight.

Similar story to team-mate Hulkenberg but just a little further back. Started 13th, finished 12th and narrowly held off Haas' Oliver Bearman at the flag.

A very good recovery after starting last because of power-unit penalties. Climbed nine positions, raced aggressively with both Audis and finished only two-tenths behind Bortoleto.

Qualified eighth and had looked set for another strong result before a fuel leak forced him to start from the pit lane. Recovering to 15th after effectively beginning the race out of contention was a decent salvage job.

The final position tells almost none of the story. Qualified fifth, started fourth and was part of the lead fight until his Red Bull front wing failed over the bumps after the safety-car restart. The pace was there for a huge result. He lost a position after the race because of a 10-second penalty for driving slowly and holding up Russell before they pitted under the safety car.

Another respectable showing in only his second grand prix for Haas. Narrowly missed Q2 and was running steadily before being spun in the Sergio Perez collision, then recovered from the back after the safety car to finish 16th.

Another difficult weekend for Aston Martin. Qualified 20th before his engine penalty pushed him further back and there was little progress to be made during the race.

Qualified at the back and Cadillac again lacked the pace to threaten the midfield. At least he stayed in the fight with the Aston Martins and made it to the finish after several recent retirements.

Aston Martin simply never looked competitive. Qualified 19th, spent the race towards the back and retired late on.

A real missed opportunity for the Briton and his Racing Bulls team. Sixth in qualifying and fifth on the grid was superb, and he was still right in the leading train when the safety car came out. Spinning while trying to warm the tyres behind it and eventually retiring was a costly unforced error.

Qualified only 18th but appeared to have better race pace and was making progress before the collision with Camara ended his afternoon.

A weekend that ended before the race even started. Qualified 16th and was due to start 14th, but overheating rear brakes on the laps to the grid caused enough damage to prevent Williams from racing the car.

articles.title: Quiles gana hasta con sustos y llega a 12 victorias en un año en Moto3
articles.standfirst: Almansa, sancionado por tocar a Brian Uriarte en la pelea por el segundo puesto
articles.summary: Almansa, sancionado por tocar a Brian Uriarte en la pelea por el segundo puesto
articles.body: Máximo Quiles ganó la carrera de Moto3 del Gran Premio de Portugal, en Portimao. El campeón alcanza las 12 victorias en este 2026 mágico para él. Supera, así, las 11 que lograra en su día Valentino Rossi en 125cc. Llovió algo por la noche y la pista estaba algo húmeda. La Dirección de Carrera decidió que la carrera fuera declarada en mojado y redujo la distancia de 19 a sólo 12 vueltas. Antes de salir la duda era auciante para todos sobre qué neumáticos usar, porque había sol, pero el asfalto no estaba del todo seco. Por eso, casi todos optaron por gomas lisas; sólo Yamanaka, que partía muy atrás, puso las rayadas. En la salida, Brian Uriarte sorprendía a todos y volaba: endosaba seis décimas al siguiente en el primer sector. Además, Almansa y Quiles se peleaban entre ellos. El cántabro pasó por primera vez por meta con una renta de 1.7 segundos. Tremendo. Veda Pratama se accidentaba en el último ángulo. La prueba se tensaba rápidamente: Brian se marchaba, Quiles lo veía y pasaba a Almansa para intentar seguirle; los cogían metros con Kelso, que había dejado de rueda a Salmela, Adrián Fernández y Carpe. Yamanaka iba diez segundos más lento que los de la cabeza, con lo que estaba claro que había elegido mal. El nipón se acabó retirando. El tirón del ya campeón hacía que la distancia con Uriarte se estabilizara en torno a los dos segundos. De paso, Máximo se iba de un Almansa que era atrapado por Fernández y Salmela, con Kelso y Carpe perdiendo comba. Quiles no se conformaba y apretaba. Así, mediada la cita, el murciano lograba reducir la diferencia a un segundo. Brian, además, se iba hasta por fuera de los pianos intentando forzar, lo que le hacía perder metros. Almansa también cambiaba de ritmo: se acercaba y pasaba a Quiles para encabezar la persecución. Fernández y Salmela igualmente estaban en el grupo. Con David en segundo lugar, la fuga se vino abajo: atrapó al del Ajo KTM. Adrián rebasó a Quiles y se permitía soñar con metas mayores. Eso sí, Máximo se la devolvía al poco. Tuvieron un toque y, por fortuna, los dos siguieron en pie. Quiles se espoleó con el contacto: adelantó a Almansa en el primer viraje y a Uriarte en el tercero. Espectacular. El del Aspar Team forzaba, pero encaró el giro final con sólo una décima de ventaja y todo por decidir. Máximo tuvo un susto tremendo, que controló de milagro para seguir hasta primero. Brian se abrió un poco y Almansa le tocó; Uriarte se cayó y Salmela aprovechó para pasar a ambos. Adrián, luego, rebasó a Almansa, que fue sancionado casi al momento con una Long Lap. Al no poder cumplirla, se le añadieron tres segundos a su crono final. Pese a ello finalizó cuarto. Brian pudo levantar su moto y cruzar la meta en sexta posición. El triunfo era para Quiles, la 12, es un animal. De paso, igualó las 15 en 125cc que tiene su jefe, Jorge Martínez Aspar. Primer podio mundialista para Salmela y Adrián suma dos seguidos. Almansa tuvo el detalle de ir al box del Ajo a disculparse con un Uriarte que estaba llorando con el casco puesto. David ató, matemáticamente, el subcampeonato. Máximo, que tuvo la fiesta de su título en Murcia hace una semana -portó una bandera de su región- quiere más. "No sé ni cómo he hecho esa salvada. Me encanta ganar en Portugal, hay muchos aficionados españoles. Ahora, a por el título de Marc Márquez", decía sobre su mentor. Almansa pedía perdón. "Me he equivocado, toqué una zona húmeda y no pude evitar impactar con Brian. Me sabe mal, porque él hizo un carrerón", afirmó.

articles.title: Las Vegas Grand Prix: Max Verstappen the constant amid chaos as he takes revenge on George Russell
articles.summary: Max Verstappen was the star figure in a Las Vegas Grand Prix that was unlike any F1 race anyone younger than about 70 had ever seen.
articles.body:
Warning: This article contains offensive language

Max Verstappen was a constant amid the chaos at a remarkable Las Vegas Grand Prix.

He was the star figure in a race that had 34 overtaking moves for the lead in 50 laps and 352 overall, in which the biggest advantage the leader ever had was 1.5 seconds, and in which there were five cars fighting nose to tail for the lead to the final lap, and for much of the race many more than that.

Even better for Verstappen, George Russell made a critical mistake 24 hours after he had revived his long-standing, on-off spat with the Dutchman.

Russell, who had been Verstappen's main threat from the start of the race, locked up his brakes and speared into the barrier trying to pass Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli for second place behind Verstappen with two laps to go.

Verstappen said: "He speaks a lot next to the track, and it doesn't really bother me because he's so far below my level that it doesn't really make any sense for me anyway to try and challenge that, you know?

"And today, karma is a bitch. It was honestly fantastic when I looked in my mirror and I saw what was happening. I was, like, "Fantastic, my day is only getting better."

"And of course, when I then crossed the line in first, my day was complete."

Verstappen wins extraordinary race as Ferraris collide

Hamilton-Leclerc collision 'completely unacceptable'

Verstappen felt motivated to make these remarks because of what Russell had said the day before.

After an on-track altercation in practice, the pair had had an exchange of views in the stewards' room. Then, after Verstappen took pole from Russell - after fastest man Antonelli's five-place penalty was taken into account - the Briton took a pop at the Dutchman.

"I am not just going to accept somebody to screw me over like this and walk around like they are bigger and better than everyone else," Russell said. "Somebody has got to stand up to that guy."

In the paddock, a number of people felt that Verstappen was probably not the right "guy" to pick a fight with.

Even though Russell was battling with Verstappen throughout the race, the nature of their drives was different.

Russell would pass the Red Bull on the straight. Then Verstappen would reclaim the lead in more extreme fashion, on the outside of the fast kink leading on to the pit straight, or on the outside again at the long Turn Three.

Hardly anyone else even tried these moves, let alone pulled them off. Verstappen made them look routine.

After his error, Russell managed to extricate himself from the crash barrier, but he had turned a certain podium finish into a ninth place.

It was the perfect encapsulation of a season in which almost nothing has gone right.

For Verstappen, it was almost too good to be true.

'It was Indy 500 and Nascar and Formula 1 mixed'

The race was unlike any grand prix anyone younger than about 70 had ever seen.

The fabled slipstreaming battles of a pre-chicane Monza in the 1960s and early 1970s - that led to the closest ever finish in F1 history at the 1971 Italian Grand Prix, , external when the first five cars crossed the line 0.6secs apart - were the closest comparison at the highest echelon of the sport.

In modern terms, it was more reminiscent of American oval racing, where the high-speed nature of the race tracks leads to long chains of cars slipstreaming and lots of overtaking, little of it meaningful until the final stages.

Mercedes F1 team boss Toto Wolff pretty much hit the nail on the head when he said: "It was Indy 500 and Nascar and Formula 1 mixed - I enjoyed it."

And it encapsulated something else about F1 2026 - the internal debate that has been raging in the sport about artificiality ever since the latest engines were introduced.

The near 50-50 split between internal combustion and electrical power has created energy-starved cars where the batteries run out before the end of long straights.

On certain tracks this has led to a form of racing known as "yo-yo", where cars constantly pass and re-pass each other depending on their respective levels of battery charge.

After a chaotic few races early in the year, this has diminished as teams have better understood energy management.

But in Las Vegas the combination of long straights and slipstreaming brought it to its apotheosis. And no-one quite knew what to think about it.

Verstappen said: "Really, really surreal and something that I've never seen before in Formula 1 myself.

"It was just a crazy amount of fighting. The slipstream was so big that you - it was just impossible to drive off, and it was just crazy how many people were just following you.

"It was just very exciting, I guess, for everyone to watch. I know, of course, it's a big show around here the whole weekend, and I hope that we delivered on track."

That was a carefully judged answer for the television cameras, the sort that sounds like one thing, but if you know the person's real views, you can read between the lines to see the nuances that hint at something else.

In the news conference, Verstappen's true feelings came out. Was it a kind of racing he enjoyed?

"When I look at it from my racer heart, not," he said. "When you look at it as a show spectacle, yes.

"I enjoyed my repassing and everything, but I prefer to look at it with my racing heart. Even my heart rate, I was not nervous at all because it's just felt kind of cruising out there, just trying to press the battery whenever it was correct or defend.

"But for the show, when you look at it from the outside, probably, yes, you like it. But, yeah, I don't know.

"I probably shouldn't say it. I probably should not. I remember winning one like this when I was playing Mario Kart.

"Sometimes you drop back and you get drafts, and there's like a catch-up, you know? Always when you're dropping back, you go faster. So that's the last time that I felt something like this."

Verstappen's superb racecraft & Russell's costly mistake - driver ratings

McLaren's Lando Norris, who finished second, said: "From a racing point of view, from the outside, I'm sure it probably was the best race ever in Formula 1.

"You never know what's going to happen. There were overtakes out of nowhere, and some of the overtakes weren't overtakes, you press boost and you go past someone. But the racing was still good. You're still fighting for position, and there are a lot of good things in there."

Russell said: "It was interesting. It was quite fun for maybe half the race, but then it started to get a bit tiring at one point because it was just absolutely impossible to get away."

Essentially, this is an argument between racing purists and casual fans, especially the new ones who know little of the complexities of the sport. Wolff related a story about his wife Susie's experience with corporate guests during the race.

"I guess you will have many people that will say that's not racing," Wolff said. "Personally, we need to be open minded.

"Susie was in the Paddock Club and she said that for 90 minutes people were screaming with the overtakes.

"The instant feedback I got from the friends watching, our sponsors, was that was awesome. Stefano [Domenicali, the F1 chairman] liked it very much. That's not going to happen everywhere."

Is F1 making a mistake in changing rules again?

Verstappen's Mario Kart comparison brought back memories of his criticisms of the new F1 in the first few races, when he said he hated it so much he was considering stopping.

Since then, the current rules have been tweaked, and more changes have been introduced for 2027 and 2028 to reduce this effect.

And, irony of ironies, this weekend it was announced that there will be new rules for 2030. These retain turbo hybrid engines but reduce the electrical element, with the express intention of removing energy starvation and making racing 'pure' again. The likely result will be that this kind of race could not be possible again after that.

In the context of Vegas, is this actually a mistake?

Wolff said: "We're still doing the right thing. It's what we all wanted. But I have no doubt people will complain there is not great overtaking. We go back to the 'glorious years' in the 2000s. But we're gonna get those regs right. We see what we can do. It just needs a kilometre and a half straight."

McLaren team principal Andrea Stella added: "It's very difficult to have a position as simple as saying, 'Oh, that's the race we want.' Because as soon as you say that, you will see some other perspectives which are important to consider.

"Like, I still have to talk to Lando and Oscar (Piastri) and understand, did you enjoy it or that was kind of too much and at times it felt like this is going to go very wrong from a safety point of view?

"So, I don't want to express a net position. Because, in fact, I don't have it.

"This race gave us a lot of information that we cannot ignore. In terms of the attention, the spectacle, in terms of, you know, like, wow, that's incredible racing, is this what we want?

"My main recommendation is that we remain kind of analytical. And we remain caring for the interest of the sport.

"Because we live in a world where everything is polarised, a world in which you need to have an opinion in one second. Otherwise you are a nobody. You need to have an opinion that is polarised.

"Well, I would like to have people that actually still value complexity of analysis. And caring for a common interest. That's my main message.

"When you have examples like today which offer so much information it would be a shame to process it in the space of a hot review. And say, 'Oh, let's abandon the new regulations.' That's not the case.

"But definitely there's some interesting information that we should consider from a technical point of view, from a sport regulation point of view."

articles.title: Manu González vive un drama, pero llegará líder a Valencia ante un Izan Guevara que depende de sí mismo
articles.standfirst: Dani Muñoz se estrenó en la victoria
articles.summary: Dani Muñoz se estrenó en la victoria
articles.body: Dani Muñoz ganó la carrera de Moto2 del Gran Premio de Portugal, en Portimao. El sevillano logró su primera victoria mundialista. El título se decidirá en Valencia. Manu González llegará líder, pero sólo con 4,5 puntos de ventaja sobre Izan Guevara después de una prueba en la que pasó de todo. Esto hace que el que se imponga en Cheste será campeón. La pista se había ido secando y la temperatura subiendo, con lo que aunque había alguna humedad, el asfalto despejaba dudas sobre qué gomas a elegir: todos con las lisas. En la salida, Agius mantenía el primer puesto de la pole. Izan bajaba del tercero al quinto. Manu ganaba una posición en la arrancada y, luego, subía al octavo, pero Alonso López le hacía pasar noveno por meta. Rueda se accidentaba. Senna tenía un trallazo y se debía abrir; esto hacía que bajara al sexto puesto. Guevara superaba a Veijer. Al poco era Holgado el que tenía un susto y cedía el primer lugar, que heredaba Dani Muñoz. El alicantino, al volver, se tocó con Ortolá y milagrosamente no se cayó. Izan era segundo y Manu se mantenía octavo, en un grupo numeroso. González se iba fuera, hasta tocando la hierba, y bajaba al 14º. Tuvo que hacer una salvada, pero rompió la cúpula. En el IntactGP contenían la respiración. ‘Manugasss’ se condenaba a buscar, de nuevo, la remontada. Empezaba adelantando a Escrig. Por arriba le iban llegando buenas noticias: Veijer rebasaba a Guevara. Sin embargo, el neerlandés tenía un susto enorme en la curva 5; lo controló, pero se debió abrir... con Izan en paralelo. Eso hizo que los adelantaran Ortolá y Alonso López. El balear sufría y le pasaban los dos de Aspar, Holgado y David Alonso. Manu subía al 12º, intentando arañar puntos. Un accidente alteró todo. En la vuelta 8, en la curva 3, con Van den Goorbergh, Salac, Sasaki y Manu González implicados. La Dirección de Carrera paró la carrera. Salac se cayó y los de detrás no pudieron evitar el impacto. Por suerte, ninguno tenía lesiones. Manu intentaba llevar su moto al box para poner retornar a la acción en la nueva salida. Varios espectadores que estaban en el vial empujaron la montura hasta el ‘pit lane’, pero por la parte trasera, donde la recogieron unos mecánicos del IntactGP, mientras que el madrileño aterrizaba en un ‘scooter’. Los miembros de IRTA le comunicaron a la escuadra alemana que Manu no podía volver, ni reparándola, al haber llegado la moto por un lugar incorrecto. Palo brutal para González. Salac tampoco podía volver. La nueva carrera se establecía a sólo siete vueltas y con las posiciones de parrilla en función del giro anterior al incidente, el séptimo. Esto daba la pole a Dani Muñoz y el octavo lugar a Guevara. En la segunda salida, Ortolá ganaba la partida a Muñoz, pero se montaba un lío al poco y Alonso López tomaba el mando. Iván pasaba de primero a cuarto. Furusato se caía. Izan, cauto, se mantenía octavo. El mallorquín rebasaba a Veijer para escalar un puesto, mientras que Muñoz superaba a López en cabeza. Guevara se topaba con su amigo Holgado, que no cedía. Baltus, que iba muy atrás, besaba el asfalto. El de Palma pronto vio que tenía peor ritmo que el de San Vicente del Raspeig. La pelea era por el tercer escalón del podio entre Ortolá, Agius y David Alonso, pues Muñoz y López se habían fugado. Dani Muñoz ganaba, delante de Alonso López, que supo tapar a Senna Agius. El andaluz se había guardado un neumático nuevo y lo supo usar a la perfección. Guevara contuvo a Huertas por apenas 44 milésimas. "Me he dejado la piel. He sufrido mucho. El susto de Veijer me hizo salir en una mala posición en la segunda carrera. Salvamos el fin de semana. Es un regalo estar donde estoy. Es una pena lo de Manu, porque no fue una caída por su culpa. Está en mis manos para Valencia", afirmaba Izan en DAZN.

articles.title: Marc Márquez, campeón de MotoGP 2026, logra el décimo
articles.standfirst: Fue conservador para hacer historia
articles.summary: Fue conservador para hacer historia
articles.body: Marc Márquez lo logró: es campeón del mundo de MotoGP en 2026. Llegó el décimo título, al fin. El que le convierte en el tercero con más de todos los tiempos, tras los 15 de Giacomo Agostini y los 12+1 de Ángel Nieto. Es un mito. La carrera la ganó Marco Bezzecchi, con Jorge Martín, segundo y Raúl Fernández firmando el triplete de Aprilia. Hasta Portimao llegó su lucha. Había numerosas bajas y sustituciones: Pol Espargaró por Maverick Viñales (Tech3 KTM), Jake Dixon por Joan Mir (Honda), Iker Lecuona por Pecco Bagnaia (Ducati oficial) y Augusto Fernández por Toprak Razgatlioglu (Prima Pramac Yamaha). Fue el día más soleado de todo el fin de semana, con lo que la pista se secó y la temperatura iba al alza, con 20 grados en el ambiente y 28 en el asfalto. Eso hizo que todos salieron con neumáticos medios delante y detrás. En la salida, Marc sorprendía a todos. En la previa dijo que se lo tomaría con calma, pero apretó y superó a Bezzecchi. Martín arrancaba muy bien para posicionarse quinto. Raúl también crecía para situarse justo detrás del ilerdense, con las dos Aprilia oficiales en su zaga. Zarco se llevaba por delante a Álex Márquez. Parecía tranquilo para el mayor de los Márquez, pero le llegó el lío: aminoró un poco y quiso abrirse para no tener problemas. Lo malo fue que no le pasó uno ni dos, sino muchos. De golpe se vio séptimo y en Ducati sudaban. Por arriba, las tres motos de Noale se fugaban, aunque con el del Trackhouse mandando. Martín era segundo y ‘Bez’, sólo tercero. El ‘93’ se veía agobiado por Binder y Di Giannantonio. Intentaba poner su ritmo y por unas vueltas tuvo algo de respiro. Acosta se caía y eso le daba un puesto más. Pero el alivio duró poco para el catalán, porque el romano se liberó del sudafricano y le pasó. Al poco, Ogura imitó al italiano. Esto ponía a Marc en octava posición. Mediada la prueba, Bezzecchi se lanzaba y superaba a Martinator en el primer ángulo. A Marc se lo indicaban, pues si no vencía Jorge, le valía con ser 14º. El de San Sebastián de los Reyes perdía algo el contacto con los otros dos de Aprilia y Marc jugaba con la calculadora, porque Binder se le arrimaba. Matemáticamente, le servía con ser noveno para no tener que mirar a las posiciones de sus contrincantes. Bezzecchi iba a lo suyo y adelantaba a Raúl en su sitio favorito: el primer ángulo. Eso sí, para mantener vivas sus opciones necesitaba que Marc no puntuara. El de Rímini mostraba lo visto en entrenamientos y se marcaba un giro brutal para hacer la vuelta rápida y fugarse de Fernández. El de San Martín de la Vega tenía problemas en la aceleración y Martín se pegó y le superó en la primera frenada. Este segundo lugar obligaba a Marc a estar entre los 14 primeros. Los fans del ‘93’ tragaban saliva, pues Binder se mantenía en la zaga del leridano... y Marini se acercaba. Hasta que Brad le pasó, lo que colocaba a Marc en noveno lugar. Dependía del hermano de Valentino Rossi el hecho de que el ilerdense bajara de su sitio de confort. En el box del Aprilia oficial hablaban y tenían la opción de dar órdenes, pues Martinator podía ganar... pero eso dejaba fuera de juego a ‘Bez’. Las vueltas iban pasando y Marc no quería lanzarse a intentar rebasar a Binder. No quería riesgos y Marini no lograba aproximarse más. En la cabeza, no había variaciones ni indicaciones externas: Bezzecchi vencía en solitario y Martín se iba de Raúl. Diogo Moreira, que iba séptimo, se accidentaba, con lo que ya daba igual lo que hiciera Marini, pues Marc ganaba una plaza en el giro final. Octavo, como su octava corona en la clase reina. Costó, pero llegó. La celebración fue genial. El '93' se dirigió a los fans. "Señores, el año pasado dije que me quedé en paz conmigo mismo; este año va por vosotros", soltó. Luego, gritó: 'Diez'. Después, Marc, con un peto con el '1', vio unas imágenes de toda su vida, subió la escalera con una cabra al lado, es el GOAT, cabra en inglés, pero que significa Greatest Of All Time (el mejor de todos los tiempos). Se abrió una puerta y salió Agostini para abrazarle.

articles.title: Así queda la clasificación de MotoGP 2026 tras Portimao: Marc Márquez, con el octavo más valioso de su trayectoria, supera a Valentino Rossi
articles.standfirst: Marco Bezzecchi rubrica el doblete en Portimao y se queda a sólo dos puntos de Jorge Martín en la pelea por el subcampeonato
articles.summary: Marco Bezzecchi rubrica el doblete en Portimao y se queda a sólo dos puntos de Jorge Martín en la pelea por el subcampeonato
articles.body: Marc Márquez ha hecho lo necesario para ser campeón mundial por décima vez (su octavo título en la clase reina) en Portugal. El de Cervera ha sufrido de lo lindo en una carrera en la que ha salido muy bien, pero en la que con el paso de las vueltas ha ido perdiendo posiciones. A la postre, le ha valido no caerse. Esas eran sus sencillas cuentas y con esa filosofía ha competido en un día que recordará toda su vida. Finalmente, el ilerdense ha visto ondear la bandera a cuadros en octavo puesto... a más de 18 segundos de Marco Bezzechi, quien ha completado un magnífico doblete de triunfos en el trazado luso. Esa posición, que no es de las habituales para un corredor que acumula a lo largo de su excelsa trayectoria 106 victorias, 173 cajones y 106 poles, nunca tuvo tanto valor como lo ha tenido este domingo de resurrección para el ilerdense. Si el sábado falló, esta vez no ha incurrido en el mismo error. Se trataba de mantenerse encima de la moto. Un plan sin fisuras que ha cumplido como el crack que es. Aprilia se ha quedado con la recompensa de un triplete en el circuito de Portimao, ya que Jorge Martín y Raúl Fernández han completado un podio copado por las RS-GP. Así las cosas, Marc se ha coronado al abandonar el recinto portugués con 439 puntos frente a los 396 de Martinator (-43) y los 394 (-45) de Bez. Hay que recordar que ya sólo quedan por conseguir como tope los 37 de la última ronda que tendrá lugar en Valencia (del 27 al 29 de noviembre). El caso es que Marc ha conseguido hacer realidad su sueño de superar en número de coronas a su némesis, Valentino Rossi merced a esos 439 puntos, una cifra que está lejos de los 545 con los que selló su noveno entorchado. Pero este Mundial es el que tiene, probablemente, más mérito de todos. En primer lugar por haber estado mermado físicamente en el arranque del certamen, luego por la doble cirugía a la que fue sometido tras su espeluznante caída en Le Mans y, en tercer lugar, por haber sido capaz de rubricar una remontada exprés para los anales de la historia del motociclismo. En suma, ya se ha ubicado en solitario en la tercera plaza en el registro de pilotos con la mayor cifra de entorchados. El primero es Giacomo Agostini con 15 (8 de 500cc y 7 de 350cc), el segundo es Ángel Nieto con 12+1 (7 de 125cc y 6 de 50cc) y Marc es cuarto con 10 (8 de MotoGP -2013, 2014, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2025 y 2026-, 1 de Moto2 -2012- y 1 de 125cc -2010-). Con el matiz de que empata en la cifra de títulos de la categoría reina con Ago. De ahí que los organizadores del campeonato le hayan etiquetado como el GOAT, cabra en inglés. De hecho, han elegido a la leyenda italiana asociado al MV Agusta para agasajar al genio de Cervera. Por último, cierra el Top 4, Vale con 9 (7 de la clase reina, 1 de 250cc y 1 de 125cc). El '93' llegó a tener una desventaja de 102 puntos con respecto al líder (Bezzecchi) cuando finalizó el gran premio disputado en Mugello. Pero su constancia y consistencia le han conducido a la gloria. Con una increíble determinación y una resiliencia infinita (siete victorias dominicales y 10 sprints ganados destacan en su hoja de servicios del curso que está agonizando) le ha dado la vuelta a la tortilla para acabar noqueando a la dupla de la casa de Noale. Por otro lado, en Cheste se resolverá quién acaba como subcampeón este curso 2026. La lucha se prevé sumamente reñida entre los dos competidores de Aprilia. Les separa sólo dos puntos, aunque parte con cierta ventaja un Bezzecchi que ha encarado la recta final del campeonato en un espléndido estado de forma. El de Rímini ha enlazado tres victorias consecutivas (las carreras dominicales de Qatar y Portugal y el Sprint disputado en el Autódromo Internacional del Algarve. Mientras que en Constructores, Aprilia afrontará la traca final con una renta escasa de 9 puntos sobre Ducati (598 Vs. 589), una vez que en la prueba corta celebrada en suelo luso ya consiguió meterse en el bolsillo el Mundial de Equipos.

articles.title: Marc Márquez logra la mayor remontada de la historia
articles.standfirst: Superó los 102 puntos de desventaja que tenía en Mugello
articles.summary: Superó los 102 puntos de desventaja que tenía en Mugello
articles.body: Hay cifras que se han quedado o se van a quedar en la memoria colectiva cuanto menos de MotoGP o de los aficionados al motociclismo. Sin duda, una va a ser 102, que son los puntos que ha tenido que remontar Marc Márquez para alzarse con su décima corona mundial, la octava en la clase reina. Todo porque se trata de la mayor remontada en la historia del Mundial... y de largo. Aquél punto más bajo llegó a la conclusión de la séptima cita del certamen de 2026, en el Gran Premio de Italia, en Mugello. Entonces, el ilerdense retornaba a la acción después de pasar por quirófano tras una caída en Le Mans. Fue sexto, frente al primer lugar de Marco Bezzecchi y el segundo de Jorge Martín. En realidad, todo empezó a girar en la prueba posterior, en Hungría. El ‘93’ ya recortó el sábado, al imponerse en el Sprint, pero el domingo todo fue más radical, al sumar él 25 puntos frente al doble cero de sus rivales de Aprilia, después del KO de ambos en la salida. Desde Balaton, todo fue una escalada que culminó en Japón, cuando igualó a Martinator por el liderato. Más adelante, tras el Sprint de Australia, donde Jorge se accidentó y Marc totalizó los 12 puntos, la renta del catalán no paró de crecer hasta permitirle atar matemáticamente el entorchado. Cabe matizar que desde 2023, en MotoGP hay carreras cortas y largas, con lo que hay más puntuación en juego. También 2026 será la temporada con más citas, por mucho que el domingo de Australia no hubiera carrera. La anterior plusmarca la tenía otro campeón con Ducati, Pecco Bagnaia, quien en 2022, le remontó 91 puntos a Fabio Quartararo y su Yamaha. Esa fue con la puntuación que se estableció en 1993, con 25 puntos al ganador dominical y sumando los 15 primeros. La tercera mayor remontada fue la de Joan Mir en 2020, al sobreponerse a un déficit de 48 puntos. Marc no es nuevo en esto de subir desde muy abajo. Así, en 2017 remontó los 37 puntos que le llegó a sacar Maverick Viñales. En 2013, también ‘levantó’ los 30 que iba por detrás. Otras muy sonadas fueron las de Jorge Lorenzo, en 2015, cuando recuperó 29 puntos a Valentino Rossi o la de Mick Doohan, quien también minimizó esa misma cifra en 1995.

articles.title: Marc Marquez wins MotoGP title: Record-equalling eighth for Spanish Ducati rider secured in Portugal
articles.summary: Marc Marquez secures a record-equalling eighth MotoGP championship and moves level with Giacomo Agostini.
articles.body:
Marc Marquez clinched a record-equalling eighth MotoGP championship with an eighth-placed finish in the Portuguese Grand Prix on Sunday.

The Spaniard needed to finish in the top nine on his Ducati to seal a second consecutive championship and move level with legendary Italian Giacomo Agostini on eight titles.

He started second on the grid and rode cautiously after crashing out in the sprint race on Saturday.

Aprilia's Italian rider Marco Bezzecchi, who held a 102-point advantage over Marquez at one stage this season, was Sunday's race winner, while Marquez's fellow Spaniards Jorge Martin and Raul Fernandez completed the top three.

But the attention was all centred around Marquez, who was hoisted in the air by his team after crossing the line.

The 33-year-old won seven grands prix and 10 sprint races this season, adding to the 11 grands prix he won in 2025.

While Sunday marked his eighth MotoGP title, it was Marquez's 10th championship overall after wins in the 125cc and Moto2 categories on his journey to the top.
